tasks.short: Teach students to use lab and workshop equipment and materials safely, supervise practicals and handle incidents.

steps.what: Teacher checks the practical's risk card and equipment with the lab technician
Students sign the lab rules: on a paper list today, by passing a short lab safety quiz in the learning environment after the change
Lab technician prepares equipment and chemicals for the practical
Teacher instructs students on goggles, chemicals, burners and tools
Teacher checks on the paper list that each student signed the lab rules
Teacher monitors students during the practical and stops unsafe use of equipment
Teacher deals with spills, breakage or minor injuries and fills an incident form: on paper today, as a digital form after the change
Teacher reports broken equipment and used chemicals: by e-mail today, in the lab's form with the practical's item list filled in after the change, entering what was actually used or broken
Teacher checks the restock request before it goes: items, quantities actually used and what is broken
Teacher submits the checked restock request to the lab technician's queue
Lab technician restocks chemicals and repairs or replaces equipment

tasks.design: A short lab safety quiz in the {LMS} replaces the paper lab-rules list, so the teacher sees who is cleared before a practical. Incidents go into a digital form, which keeps its time as a first record. A form per lab in the {HELPDESK} lists the practical's items; the teacher enters what was used or broken, checks the request and submits it once to the lab technician; instruction and supervision are unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety records were paper lists and notes because volumes are small.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments run quizzes with completion lists, and helpdesk forms are quick to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Safety in a lab depends on the teacher's attention to thirty students at once.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the student who is about to do something dangerous and stopping it calmly.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; fewer paper lists and notes.

reach.learn: Whether item lists from the form make restocking faster.

evidence.claim: Learning environments can run a quiz and show completion per student.
Lab safety and handling of hazardous substances in schools follow national workplace safety rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing a practical to restocking after it; lesson content is outside.
Input contract: safety quiz completion produced by students in the {LMS} (their time is outside the teacher's savings); risk cards kept by the lab technician; fallback is the paper list.
Lab technician time is outside the teacher's savings.
Instruction and supervision do not change.

Students' quiz is shown in s9 at share 1. Handling incidents and filling the form keep their full time. s7 keeps 70 because the teacher still enters actual quantities and breakages; the check and submission keep their full time.
unknowns: How many practicals a teacher runs per week.
Whether risk cards exist per practical.
research_questions: Do students who pass a safety quiz cause fewer lab incidents?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks the quiz completion list before the practical.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the safety quiz current with the lab rules.
Students' extra time for the yearly quiz beyond signing the list.

approvals.approved_version: The restock request with items, quantities used and breakages exactly as checked by the teacher in s7b, submitted once to the lab technician's queue in the helpdesk; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many students skip the quiz so the paper list stays (s4 at 60) and the item list rarely fits (s7 at 90) (2.2); high: quiz and lab form used as designed (4.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work with the section and school leaders to evaluate and revise subject programmes using exam results and feedback.

steps.what: Teacher joins section meetings on the development of the subject programs
Teacher compiles school-exam and central-exam grades and pass rates per subject
Students fill in the course evaluation form in the learning environment
Teacher reads student course evaluations and colleagues' remarks

loop.input: Open answers from the student course evaluation, without names.
loop.output: Topic themes with the answer IDs behind each theme.
loop.check: Each theme cites at least three answer IDs containing its key words; counts are computed from IDs; quotes match the source; the teacher reads the cited answers for each theme and checks the theme says what they say; answers left unthemed are read in full; no theme labels students' feelings.
loop.stop: One pass per evaluation; under 30 answers the raw list is shown instead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Hundreds of open answers use varied words; keyword counts miss most themes.

steps.what: Teacher drafts proposed changes to the programme and testing
Section head and school leader decide on the revision
Teacher updates programme documents and next year's testing programme
Teacher checks the revised programme documents and testing programme: they contain exactly the revisions decided
Teacher publishes the checked programme documents for the section

tasks.design: A standard exam-results view in {BI} shows school-exam and central-exam grades, their gap and pass rates per subject and cohort; student course evaluations run as an {LMS} form whose open answers a bounded model step groups into themes tied to answer IDs. A proposal template pre-fills the figures. After the section head's decision the teacher updates the documents, checks them against the decision and publishes them once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each evaluation began with exports and spreadsheets, and open answers were read one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Exam results can feed a standard dashboard, and language models group open answers when a check ties themes to sources.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what to change is a section judgement; results views per teacher can feel like monitoring.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting what the figures mean for this school's students and getting colleagues to agree on a change.

ambition.what: Every subject reviews its school-exam and central-exam gap each year with the same view.

tasks.altitude: The teacher spends section time on causes and choices; the section head decides from consistent material.

reach.learn: Which subjects show a lasting gap between school and central exam grades.

evidence.claim: Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff, which can include results per teacher.
Inferring pupils' emotions with AI is banned, so the theme step classifies topics only.
The gap between school-exam and central-exam grades is a standard quality indicator for Dutch secondary schools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the section's evaluation work to revised programme documents; implementation in class is outside.
Input contract: school-exam and central-exam grades produced by the exam secretary in the student information system; course evaluations filled by students in the {LMS}; fallback is a manual export.
Results are shown per subject and cohort, not per teacher, unless the staff council agrees.
Section head and student time is outside the teacher's savings.

Students' form time is shown in s7 at share 1. s3 keeps 60 because the teacher reads the cited answers per theme and all unthemed answers. Updating the documents (s6) keeps its full time; the check and publication keep theirs.
unknowns: Whether course evaluations are run per subject today.
Whether exam data can be exported after results.
research_questions: Does a yearly results view lead sections to change their testing programmes?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks the results view figures before using them.
Teacher checks themes against a sample of answers.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps evaluation questions and the proposal template current.
School data staff maintain the results view and model service.

approvals.approved_version: The programme documents and next year's testing programme with exactly the revisions decided in s5, as checked by the teacher in s6b, published once to the section; any other change needs a new decision and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small subject with too few evaluations to theme and a section that mostly discusses, so s3 and s4 keep 90 (13.5); high: results view, themes and template used as designed (21.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare lessons for each class: plans, materials and quizzes, upload them, and show plans when asked.

steps.what: Teacher reviews the course outline for next week's lessons per class
Teacher reads the textbook chapter and teacher guide to prepare classes
Teacher writes a lesson plan per class: objectives, activities, timing
Teacher makes worksheets and a quiz, with versions per level

loop.input: Lesson objectives, the textbook section and the class level.
loop.output: A short quiz with answer key and a worksheet per level.
loop.check: Each question maps to an objective; answers are recomputed or found in the textbook section; a word list checks level; the teacher reads every item against the textbook section for correctness and level and drops items that are wrong or unclear.
loop.stop: One redraft; then the teacher writes the material.
loop.why_not_simpler: New questions and level variants need writing; a question bank covers only part of the course.

steps.what: Teacher checks the final materials before students get them: content right, answer keys right, versions for the right classes
Teacher uploads the checked lesson materials for students: by hand today, one release to the class pages after the change
Section head reads lesson plans during a lesson visit

tasks.design: Lesson plans per class are pre-filled in {DOCS} from the course outline in the {LMS} (objectives, chapter, homework), and a bounded model step drafts quizzes and level variants from the objectives and textbook section. After the teacher's final check, the teacher releases the materials once to the class pages in the {LMS}, and plans stay available for lesson visits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans and materials were typed per class, and level variants doubled the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments hold course outlines, and trials with secondary teachers showed AI-assisted planning saves time without lower quality.
tasks.still_hard: Thinking through the lesson cannot be skipped, and drafted questions can be wrong or too easy.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipating where this class will struggle and planning how to keep them engaged.

ambition.what: Students in mixed-level classes who get a version at their level every lesson.

tasks.altitude: The teacher reviews pre-filled plans and drafted materials; preparation time shifts to thinking the lesson through.

reach.task: Teach a class from the regular teacher's plan
reach.learn: Whether pre-filled plans in the LMS are enough to teach from.

evidence.claim: A randomised trial with 259 secondary science teachers cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with a chatbot and guide, with no quality difference.
A Dutch lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
A school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from reviewing the outline to materials published; teaching the lessons is outside.
Input contract: course outline with objectives and chapters per week, produced in the course-outline task and kept in the {LMS}; textbook sections the school licenses; fallback is the blank template.
No pupil data goes into the draft step.
Section head time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether the textbook licence allows its text in a model service.
How many classes and levels a teacher prepares per week.
research_questions: After ten weeks, for what share of lessons do teachers still use drafted quizzes?

already_counted.description: Teacher edits the pre-filled lesson plan.
Teacher reviews drafted quizzes and level variants before use.

incremental.description: Teacher reports poor drafts and keeps the outline current.
School IT keeps the template and model service running.

approvals.approved_version: The lesson materials and answer keys exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, released once to the named class pages in the learning environment; edits after the check need a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: as uptake in trials suggests, teachers use drafts for only some lessons, so s4 keeps 90 and mainly the pre-filled plans save (26.9); high: drafts used for most lessons (36.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find, get approval for, attend and record professional training, conferences and meetings.

steps.what: Teacher looks for relevant training, conferences and workshops
Teacher requests approval and budget from the school leader
School leader approves the training and budget
Teacher checks the enrolment before it goes: course, dates and cost as the school leader approved
Teacher registers for the event: by e-mail or the organiser's site today, by one enrolment from the catalogue after the change
Teacher prepares the cover request for missed lessons: listed by hand today, generated from the timetable after the change
Teacher checks the cover request before it goes: the missed lessons, classes and work to set
Teacher sends the checked cover request to the timetabler
Timetabler arranges substitutes for the missed lessons
Teacher attends the training, conference or professional meeting
Teacher records hours and certificates in the development file
Teacher shares what was learned in a section meeting

tasks.design: A training request form in the {LMS} or {HCM} with the school's course catalogue routes approval to the school leader; once approved, the teacher checks the enrolment and sends it once, and checks the cover request generated from the timetable data before sending it once to the timetabler. Certificates uploaded after the event fill the teacher's development record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests, budgets and cover ran by e-mail, and development records were personal files.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning and HR systems hold catalogues, approvals and records, and timetables can list the lessons a date affects.
tasks.still_hard: External conferences still need manual registration; attending and applying what was learned is the point.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to learn for their own teaching and bringing it back to colleagues.

ambition.what: Development plans reviewed against actual training in every yearly appraisal, from the same record.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less e-mail around each course.

reach.learn: Which catalogue courses teachers actually request.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can hold a course catalogue with request and approval flows and completion records.
Teachers' professional development hours are set in the collective agreement; details follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from looking for training to sharing what was learned; designing the school's training programme is outside.
Input contract: course catalogue kept by HR or the school academy; timetable data from the timetabler; certificates uploaded by the teacher; fallback is e-mail.
School leader and timetabler time is outside the teacher's savings.
Attending the training does not change.
Enrolling and preparing the cover request keep 50 each; the checks and the cover send keep their full time. s7 keeps 50 for uploading certificates, so that is not counted again as new work.
unknowns: Whether the school has a course catalogue in a system.
How many training days a teacher takes per year.
research_questions: Do teachers take more relevant training when a catalogue and quick approval exist?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; uploading certificates is part of s7.

approvals.approved_version: The enrolment for the course, dates and cost exactly as approved by the school leader in s3 and checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the course provider; another course or a higher cost needs a new approval.
The cover request with the missed lessons, classes and work to set exactly as checked by the teacher in s4d, sent once to the timetabler; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a teacher who mainly attends external conferences outside the catalogue keeps manual search, registration and cover lists, so s1 keeps 90 and s4 and s4c keep 100 (6.6); high: catalogue courses as designed (13.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps teaching, supervising and section debate; plans, materials, evaluations and paperwork shift to review.
skills_to_grow: Reviewing drafted materials for accuracy and level
Reading exam results views with colleagues
Keeping lesson plans current in the learning environment
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who prepares level-appropriate materials for every class, reviews programmes yearly from results, and plans development from a clear record.

job.title: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
